title: C482/53/2022 of RAVI PATHAK Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.53 of 2022
Ravi Pathak .......Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & another
 .....Respondents
Mr. Amit Kapri, Advocate for the applicant.
Mrs. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Deep Prakash Bhatt, Advocate, for the private respondent.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
This C482 Application, which is accompanied with the
Compounding Application i.e. IA No.01 of 2022, preferred under
section 320 of the CrPC, this is an application, which is being jointly
filed by the parties to the proceedings seeking the composition of the
offences for which the present applicant is being tried in
Criminal Case no.824 of 2021 (Session Trial No.15 of 2021) "State
vs. Ravi Pathak", for his involvement in the commission of the
offences under sections 307, 504, 506 of the IPC and under sections
4/25 of the Arms Act.
2. This court is being conscious of the fact that the
offences, which are being sought to be compounded, will not be
compoundable, as having not been included in the list as appended to
section 320 of the CrPC.
3. The matter was taken up yesterday, and the court felt that
there is some foul play, which is being played upon the victim thereby
forcing her to enter into the compounding of the offences. Hence, this
Court called upon the parties to appear in chamber. I have interacted
with the victim as well as father of both the parties, who after
prolonged interaction by the Court has made a statement that the
composition application has been filed owing to the feudalistic system
of the Indian society, which is still prevailing in the rural areas of the
country, where a female young girl for no fault of her's, who meets

2
with such type of an untoward accident or incident, which has been
caused, by the applicant is being victimized, not only by the society,
but unethically also, she has been secluded by her own family
members, without any protection being provided to her from her own
parents, rather the parents and the society in which she is presently
surviving, they are treating her as to be a girl without any chastity, but
she also submitted that since at present she is pursuing her post
graduation; she wants to resolve the controversy and bring it to quites,
and lay the proceedings at rest so that she may be able to pursue her
academics which she is presently venturing into.
4. This Court thereafter called upon the father of the victim
and the father of the applicant, namely, Mr. Kishan Pant and Mr.
Prakash Chandra Pathak. It seems that the parents of the applicant are
nothing but they are jointly colliding together with their other
relatives to exert pressure on the victim, and that is why during the
course of the conciliation, the efforts which was made by the court
Mr. Prakash Chandra Pathak, who was accompanied with one of his
close relative Mr. Prem Ballabh Pant, who in fact was an unnecessary
party, who was declined to be heard by this Court, as he was not a
necessary party, who was at all required to be heard for the purposes
of carrying of the mediation. But what has been reflected during the
course of the mediation, as per the joint statement made by Mr.
Prakash Chandra Pathak, and Mr. Kishan Pant, they submitted that
owing to the intervention of the villagers, they have entered into an
agreement (copy of which was presented during mediation) by
executing the same on the non judicial stamp paper, by virtue of a
notarized affidavit settling the terms of the settlement, which has been
duly signed by Mr. Gaurav Pant, Mr. Prakash Chandra Pathak and
Smt. Kamla Pathak.
5. This affidavit, which has been said to have been
executed between the parties, was called upon to be placed on record,
which was supplied by the father of the applicant, which is taken on
record, and will constitute as to be the part of this C482 Application.

3
6. The fact, which had emerged from the records of the
C482 Application are that owing to a friendly relationship which the
victim developed with the applicant, which cannot be said to be an
unreckoning feature in the modern society, where major young boys
and girls are at liberty to enter into a friendly relationship with one
another, and merely this act of entering into a friendly relationship
will not be stigmatic in any nature whatever, so far it relates to the
present applicant the victim, and on that pretext that the incident or
the accident, which has chanced whereby the applicant has stabbed
the victim, will not attach any personnel stigma to the character of the
victim, as there is nothing on record or even in the agreement that she
had ever indulge herself in any activity, which is not recognized by
the society and hereby as a consequence of the composition of the
offences, she will be permitted by her parents to live her free life
according to her wisdom and desire with intact chastity. Since being
major no restrictions be it even social or personal could at all be
imposed upon by the parents of the respondent No 2. This was the
expression, which was parted by the victim, when this Court was
interacting with her, that she was constrained to compound the
offence, because she was being maltreated by her own family
members, and she was left all alone with no one coming forward for
her assistance, it was rather the embarrassment caused by her own
family members and other villagers.
7. Looking to the supplementary medical report which has
been submitted by the Medical Officer on 24th April 2021, this Court,
ought to have rejected the compounding application and the applicant
should have been directed to be left open to face the trial, as the
injuries which was suffered by the victim was referred to be grievous
in nature by the medical experts, but exclusively considering the
expression given by the victim because of the duress being exercised
by the villagers and her own family members, coupled with the fact
that looking to the economic status of the family, since she wanted to
pursue her higher studies and live without any botheration, this Court
is of the view that looking to the peculiar circumstances of the present

4
case, the compounding application deserves to be accepted not in the
interest of the applicant, but rather in the interest of the victim.
8. Owing to the aforesaid reasoning, and in order to provide
a conducive environment to the victim to live with her family and
freely pursue her academic career, and freely live in the village, the
offence is compounded by exercising my inherent powers under
Section 482 of the CrPC. As a consequence thereto, the Criminal Case
no.824 of 2021 (Session Trial No.15 of 2021) "State vs. Ravi
Pathak", would hereby dropped.
9. This Court cannot be oblivions of the fact, that as a
consequence of the withdrawal of the criminal proceedings Mr. Ravi
Pathak, and his allies, which would be inclusive of her parents and
relatives may not take an advantage of composition of the offence in
future by exerting pressure on the victim or his family members, they
are all by virtue of this judgment, warned to not to indulge any such
activities, otherwise it will be open for the victim to file an
appropriate application before this Court for taking an action against
the applicant, and his parents or the allies, if they ever endeavour to
exert pressure on the victim.
10. Subject the aforesaid, the C482 Application is hereby
allowed.
